2 · Paste the post copy

24 days.

Then Alaska's primary narrows a field of 17 who would write its AI rules. Reports made public this week show Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins with the largest reported haul, 1.8 million dollars, most from Lower 48 donors per the Anchorage Daily News. Six Anthropic employees gave 372,000 of it.

Matt Heilala gave his own campaign more than 1.4 million, more than those six combined. Kreiss-Tomkins says most of his national donors have one agenda, whether he can win.

The money is compelled by law. The AI answers are not.

Disclosure, this deck was built with a Claude model made by Anthropic, those six donors' employer.

Inside, five hauls at one scale, four candidates who skipped a June AI survey, and six blanks for your candidate.

Before August 18, would you vote for a candidate who left June's AI questions blank?

#AlaskaGovernor2026 #CampaignFinance #AIPolicy

3 · Post, then paste this as the FIRST comment (within a minute)

Sources for today's deck, Alaska.Ai No. 17.

Disclosure first. This deck was produced by a routine running on a Claude model built by Anthropic, and six Anthropic employees are the donors at the center of this story. No source reports any donor's motive, no source reports any involvement by Anthropic the company, this deck asserts no causation, and no wrongdoing has been alleged in this reporting. Every figure below is from reporting you can read yourself.

A note on sourcing. The fundraising figures come from ONE article by ONE reporter, published by the Anchorage Daily News on July 23 2026 and republished by Alaska Public Media on July 24. That is one reporting source, not two independent ones.

1. Anchorage Daily News, July 23 2026, Iris Samuels, on the 1.8 million dollar haul, the 372,000 dollars from six Anthropic employees, the 100,000 dollar largest single gift, and Matt Heilala's 1.4 million dollars of his own money
https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/07/23/democrat-in-alaskas-governor-race-reports-18-million-fundraising-haul-driven-by-californians/

2. Alaska Public Media, July 24 2026, the republication carrying the six named AI regulations and the "can you win" quote
https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/elections/2026-07-24/democrat-in-alaskas-governor-race-reports-1-8-million-fundraising-haul-driven-by-californians

3. Northern Journal with the Anchorage Press, June 25 2026, Nathaniel Herz, the candidate AI survey behind slides 03, 07 and 08, labeled background throughout the deck
https://www.northernjournal.com/alaska-governors-race-survey-ai-policy-and-news-sources/

4. Air and Space Forces Magazine, April 11 2026, on the 4,700 acres offered at JBER, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station
https://www.airandspaceforces.com/usaf-land-ai-data-centers-three-alaska-bases/

5. The federal solicitation record for AFCEC-26-R-0006, showing offers due June 29 2026 and no award recorded
https://www.highergov.com/contract-opportunity/rflp-artificial-intelligence-ai-data-center-deve-afcec-26-r-0006-o-db695/

What we could NOT verify, stated plainly. There is no published in state versus out of state split for this campaign, so the deck draws none. The August 18 primary date rests on news reporting rather than on a page we could fetch from the Division of Elections. The "about a fifth" figure on slide 02 is our own arithmetic, 372,000 divided by 1.8 million, and it is labeled as such on the slide.

Editor's note

The deck's criterion arithmetic came to a raw 8.22, comfortably over the 8.0 threshold that applies at this revision round, but the score was capped at 6.9 by two hard fails from one geometry bug. Every cited instance has since been fixed and re-verified at feed scale, and machine QA is a clean PASS with zero warnings. The cap stands in the record because the rubric caps scoring at two cycles and both were spent, so no third scorer pass confirmed the repair. Read that as an honest process limit rather than a hidden defect. What a human should still check before posting: the mono label on slide 04 reading HEILALA 1.6 M, 1.4 M HIS OWN at 100 percent, because a transposed candidate name is the one defect that would be unrecoverable in public. The story itself is sound. Every honesty gate passes, both mandatory counter-framings shipped, the conflict of interest is disclosed four times, the PDF is vector with the title set, and the caption is clean at 874 chars with exactly three hashtags and no links.

The routine modified its own machinery this run. If a later week looks worse, this dated section is the rollback trail (each set reverts as one commit).
KindChangeRollback
fix
engine		qa.py gains glyph_ink_contamination(), a FAIL-grade detector for a label CROSSED by canvas/SVG/GL geometry, and busy_art_under_text() loses its font_px>=30 restriction so labels of ANY size are sampled. The new check samples a thin ring around every non-decorative label's glyph ink (skips 2px of anti-aliasing, out to 5px), takes the local paper value from outside that ring, and counts ring pixels closer to the GLYPH's own value than to paper. FAIL when that contaminated fraction >= 0.07 AND it spans >= 30 percent of the label's columns or rows; WARN from 0.02; data-overlap-ok demotes the FAIL to a WARN as with the DOM collision gate. It measures the DEFENSE rather than the busyness, so a knockout plate, a dark-ground scrim or a halo leaves the ring clean (a halo is the opposite value by construction) while a rule, scored outline, groove edge or GL specular running through the letterforms trips it. Documented in SKILL.md as a slide-contract rule (text over art needs a declared defense).

Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11 am Alaska time. This deck is dated, so sooner is better, the primary is August 18.
  • Paste the first comment immediately, within about 60 seconds of posting. It carries the disclosure and every source.
  • Reply substantively to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. A dead first hour is rarely recovered.
  • Do not add links to the post body. Sources live in the first comment only.
  • Upload the PDF as a document post and set the document title exactly as given.
  • READ THIS ONE FIRST. This deck is about political donations by six Anthropic employees and it was produced by a Claude model built by Anthropic. The disclosure is on slide 09 and in the first comment. Decide for yourself whether to post it.
